entities.summary:
The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) is a military alliance of several post-Soviet states, evolving from the 1992 Collective Security Treaty into a formal organisation headquartered in Moscow. It offers mutual defence and crisis-response mechanisms among Russia and partner states such as Belarus, Armenia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan (membership has fluctuated).

CSTO exercises, peacekeeping deployments, and political consultations reflect Moscow’s effort to institutionalise security influence after NATO expansion and regional colour revolutions. Its credibility has been tested by limited responses to members’ conflicts.

As a post-Soviet alliance, the CSTO illustrates competitive regional security architecture in Eurasia beside NATO and bilateral basing deals.
